prompt.context: Our client is a large financial services firm with multiple locations around the world. Part of their service offering includes a 24-hour helpline. The client has their call centers in New York and Paris. The client has recently acquired a small firm (Firm B) in order to expand its reach in a particular geography. Firm B provides a subset of the services and has its call center located in the Philippines.
prompt.question: The client has asked us to determine its strategy going forward for handling customer calls. In particular they want us to look into the call center operations.

clarifying_info.q: What services does the client provide?
clarifying_info.a: The client provides a full range of financial services for individuals and small organizations.

clarifying_info.q: How established is the acquired firm?
clarifying_info.a: The acquired firm was started 5 years ago and is still run by the original founders.
New employees are college graduates with basic knowledge of financial services and products. Fluency in English and several European languages is required.

It is very difficult to lay off employees in the Paris location and significant costs will be incurred. The Philippines government encourages investment in the country and significant tax advantages are possible.

exhibits.title: Call Center Performance FY 2010
exhibits.shows: A table comparing the three call center locations across calls per year, employee cost per year, overhead cost per year, and number of employees.

framework: Evaluate existing cost structure: compare cost-per-call and calls-per-employee across all three locations
Identify the most cost-effective configuration to handle total call volume
Model outsourcing scenarios with one-time transition costs and breakeven analysis
Explore efficiency improvement levers (best-practice transfer to Philippines)
Assess qualitative/strategic considerations: regulatory constraints, culture, customer satisfaction, reputational risk
Provide a recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit A, compare the three call center locations. What is the cost per call and calls per employee for each location? What is the total current cost across all centers?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate: NY calls/employee = 600,000/75 = 8,000; Paris = 400,000/60 ≈ 6,667; Philippines = 300,000/75 = 4,000. Philippines operates at half the efficiency of NY on a per-employee basis. Cost per call: NY total cost = 75*50k + 450k = $4.2M, 4.2M/600k = $7.00/call; Paris = 60*50k + 600k = $3.6M, 3.6M/400k = $9.00/call; Philippines = 75*20k + 300k = $1.8M, 1.8M/300k = $6.00/call. Total current cost across all three = $9.6M. Philippines is cheapest per call even at current lower efficiency.

math.setup: Total calls = 600,000 (NY) + 400,000 (Paris) + 300,000 (Philippines) = 1,300,000. Total cost = $9.6M (given). Calls per employee: NY = 600k/75 = 8,000; Paris = 400k/60 ≈ 6,667; Philippines = 300k/75 = 4,000.
math.answer: Philippines has the lowest cost per call ($6.00) but operates at half the efficiency of NY (4,000 vs 8,000 calls/employee/year). Total current cost = $9.6M.

questions.prompt: If the client consolidates all call volume (1.3M calls/year) to the Philippines at current efficiency, how many employees are needed and what is the new operating cost? What are the net savings vs. status quo?
questions.guidance: At current Philippines efficiency of 4,000 calls/employee/year, candidate should calculate employees needed and new total cost including overhead. One-time transition cost of $5M (severance for NY/Paris, expanding Philippines facility) must be factored in to assess profitability.

math.setup: Philippines efficiency = 4,000 calls/employee/year. Total calls = 1,300,000. Assume overhead is variable.
steps: Overhead scales proportionally: original Philippines OH rate = $300,000/75 employees = $4,000/employee, so new OH = 325 * $4,000 = $1,300,000
Conclusion: outsourcing at current efficiency is NOT profitable within 2 years
math.answer: 325 employees needed; new operating cost = $7.8M; annual savings = $1.8M; but $5M one-time cost means breakeven in ~2.8 years, which fails the 2-year requirement.

questions.prompt: The client requires a 2-year breakeven. How could the Philippines be made more cost-effective? If Philippines achieves the same efficiency as New York (8,000 calls/employee/year), what is the new cost and savings?
questions.guidance: Guide interviewee toward transferring best practices from NY to Philippines to close the efficiency gap. Candidate should recalculate headcount and costs at 8,000 calls/employee/year, with overheads doubling due to better equipment needs. Savings must now justify $5M one-time cost within 2 years.

math.setup: Philippines achieves NY efficiency = 8,000 calls/employee/year. Total calls = 1,300,000. Overheads double (better equipment): original Philippines OH = $300,000 for 75 employees handling 300,000 calls. New OH = $600,000 / 300,000 calls * 1,300,000 calls = $2,600,000 (i.e., OH doubles per interviewer guidance).
steps: Breakeven on $5M one-time cost = $5,000,000 / $3,800,000 ≈ 1.32 years — within 2-year threshold
Conclusion: outsourcing WITH efficiency improvement IS feasible
math.answer: 160 employees needed; new total cost = $5.8M; annual savings = $3.8M vs. status quo; breakeven on $5M one-time cost ≈ 1.3 years, meeting the 2-year requirement.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative risks and considerations should the client evaluate before deciding to fully outsource to the Philippines?

categories.name: Operational / Capacity Risk
ideas: Scaling Philippines capacity by more than 200% in a short time frame is operationally challenging
Risk of service quality degradation during ramp-up
Knowledge transfer gaps — complex financial services topics may be difficult to train rapidly

categories.name: Regulatory & Legal
ideas: Very difficult to lay off Paris employees; significant severance costs required
NY layoffs also carry legal and contractual obligations
Timeline for legal workforce reduction may not align with transition timeline

categories.name: People & Culture
ideas: Acquired firm (Firm B) is still run by original founders — integration and culture alignment is uncertain
Fluency in English and European languages required — talent pool in Philippines may need screening
Employee morale impact on NY/Paris staff during transition period

categories.name: Customer & Reputational Risk
ideas: Customers may notice a change in service quality or accent — satisfaction risk
Competitors could leverage the outsourcing announcement to attract clients
Public opinion impact from perceived offshoring of jobs
Financial services clients may have concerns about data privacy and security with offshore handling

categories.name: Strategic Feasibility
ideas: Can the Philippines location recruit 160+ qualified, multilingual college graduates in 3-6 months?
Best-practice transfer assumes NY processes are well-documented — this may not be the case
Tax advantages from Philippines government could partially offset transition costs

recommendation: Recommend proceeding with outsourcing to the Philippines, contingent on implementing a structured best-practice transfer program that brings Philippines efficiency up to New York levels (8,000 calls/employee/year)

Under this scenario, annual operating cost drops to $5.8M (savings of $3.8M/year vs. current $9.6M), and the $5M one-time transition cost breaks even in approximately 1.3 years — within the 2-year threshold
Retain a minimal Paris presence near-term given regulatory constraints on layoffs; phase out as legal obligations are met
risks: Talent acquisition risk: hiring 160+ multilingual college graduates in the Philippines within 3-6 months may not be feasible
Service quality risk during the transition period could hurt customer retention
Reputational risk from visible large-scale offshoring, potentially exploited by competitors
Regulatory delay in Paris could extend the transition timeline and reduce year-1 savings
Integration risk with the acquired firm's founders and culture
next_steps: Assess Philippines infrastructure requirements and timeline to expand physical facility
Conduct talent market analysis to determine feasibility of rapid hiring in the Philippines
Document and package NY best practices for structured knowledge transfer
Engage legal counsel in France and New York to map the fastest compliant path to workforce reduction
Develop a customer communication plan to proactively address service continuity concerns
Establish KPIs for call quality and customer satisfaction during the ramp-up period
